title: I’ve been building minesweeper.life, & I could really use some fresh eyes. Here’s what’s there so far.
author: raiinman1
selftext:
**TL;DR:** I’m building [minesweeper.life](https://minesweeper.life/) and need testers outside my friends group. There’s classic and no-guess Minesweeper, multiplayer, learning tools, a screenshot solver, puzzle creation, and optional goals and profile cosmetics. It’s still a work in progress, and I’ve reached the point where I need fresh eyes. Play a few games or poke around, then tell me what’s fun, confusing, broken, or missing. You don’t need to test everything or write a detailed report. Even one thing you notice would help.

[DON'T forget to check out the original 1977 minesweeper arcade](https://minesweeper.life/original/), remade in 3D as a 1:1 parity (still working on it) original game sounds, controls, and even ambient 70's arcade sound effect.

# Hello!

I’ve been working on [**minesweeper.life**](https://minesweeper.life/), and I’m finally asking people outside of myself and my friends to give it a try.

I’m honestly not great at asking for help. I’ve been putting this off, but there’s only so much I can find by testing my own site. I know where everything is, what the buttons mean, and how I expect things to work. That doesn’t tell me what it’s like for someone arriving for the first time.

# What is it?

It’s a browser-based Minesweeper site built around **playing, learning, studying boards, creating puzzles, and playing with other people**.

Classic Minesweeper is still the center of it. You can just open a board and play. The other tools are there if you want to understand a position, practice a deduction, make something yourself, or bring a friend.

Visually, I’m going for a modern arcade feel with a little personality. There’s a mascot named **Sweeps**, a dark appearance, an optional softer daytime appearance, and high contrast and color support options. Some artwork is temporary, and the presentation is still being worked on.

**It’s a working beta, and it absolutely still needs testing.** Having a page or feature available doesn’t mean I think it’s finished.

# What can you play?

[**Regular Minesweeper**](https://minesweeper.life/play/)

* **Beginner:** 9 × 9, 10 mines.
* **Intermediate:** 16 × 16, 40 mines.
* **Expert:** 30 × 16, 99 mines.
* **Classic:** the smaller 8 × 8, 10-mine board.
* **No-guess boards**, where the generator verifies a logical solving path
* **Shared boards**, so someone else can try the same layout.
* **Custom:** choose your own dimensions and mine count.

The current controls includes flagging, chording, touch controls, focus/fullscreen options, and local history and personal bests.

I’d especially like to know how the controls feel on different devices. Something feeling natural with my mouse doesn’t tell me how it feels on your phone.

# Learning and practice

The [**Learn section**](https://minesweeper.life/learn/) has an interactive introduction, starter pattern exercises with hints, and practice bots that explain their moves.

If you’re new, I want you to be able to get started without already knowing Minesweeper terminology. If you’re experienced, I’d like to know where the explanations need more detail or precision.

“I read xyz and still didn’t understand it” is useful feedback.

# The Solver

The [**Solver**](https://minesweeper.life/solver/) lets you paint in a board position or import a screenshot, review the recognized tiles, and analyze it.

It can identify forced safe moves, forced mines, and exact mine probabilities based on the visible clues and total mine count. There’s also an **experimental move-comparison mode**.

A couple of things worth explaining:

* Screenshot recognition runs in your browser. The image isn’t uploaded for recognition.
* You should review the imported board before analyzing it, because recognition can get tiles wrong.
* A real guessing position can still require a guess. The solver can’t magically find information the clues don’t provide.

This is one of the areas where I’d really appreciate experienced players trying awkward positions and telling me whether the results and explanations make sense.

# Making and sharing puzzles

[Board Studio](https://minesweeper.life/board-studio/) lets you place mines, playtest your board, and share it with someone. It’s free and doesn’t require signing in.

There’s also a [Puzzle Studio](https://minesweeper.life/studio/) for creating puzzle packs and sharing published versions, plus a [Mistake Notebook](https://minesweeper.life/notebook/) for revisiting positions you want to study.

I’d love feedback on the difference between these tools, too. If you open them and think “why are these separate?” or can’t tell which one you need, that’s something I need to hear.

# Multiplayer

[**Multiplayer**](https://minesweeper.life/multiplayer/) is currently **free and unranked**.

The available room options include:

* **Race:** separate boards with the same layout. First clear wins.
* **Solve together:** work on one shared board.
* **Team relay:** take turns revealing, with the option to hand off.
* **Party races:** race with up to eight players.

You can create a room and send someone the code. Rooms can also allow spectators.

If you have someone willing to try a match with you, feedback on joining, getting ready, starting, playing, and finishing would be a huge help. Those little transitions matter just as much as whether the board itself works.

# Accounts, community, and optional goals

There are player accounts for saving results and progression, optional public profiles, a separate opt-in player directory, clubs, and community features.

The **Playbook** gives you optional Starter Goals. You choose one at a time, can switch or pause, and keep your saved progress. These goals don’t expire or punish you for missing a day.

You’ll also see **Chips and Stars**, earned rewards used for profile cosmetics such as badges, frames, and banners. Those cosmetics don’t change your board or give you a gameplay advantage.

You can start with a regular solo board without making an account. If you do create one, **save your recovery code**. Player accounts currently don’t collect an email address, so there isn’t an email password-reset option.

# There’s also a Museum

This is a slightly different corner of the project that I’m interested in.

The [**Museum**](https://minesweeper.life/museum/) looks at Amutech’s **1977 Mine Sweeper**, an arcade naval game involving ships and mine trails. It’s a different game from numbered-cell Minesweeper.

There are cabinet photographs, period sales materials, sources, and preservation research. The original-game player currently requires an invite, so visiting the Museum doesn’t automatically give access to that.

# What’s unfinished or still coming?

There are rough edges, temporary graphics, and parts of the navigation and explanations that probably make more sense to me than they will to you.

Ranked leagues and the broader competition features are still ahead. More learning material and improvements to the existing tools are part of the longer-term plan, too.

I’m avoiding promising dates here. Right now, I need to understand how the current site behaves for people who haven’t been watching it develop.

# What kind of help am I asking for?

**Pick whatever interests you. You don’t need to test the whole site.**

Play a few boards. Try a lesson. Put a difficult position into the solver. Make a puzzle. Race a friend. Or just look around and tell me where you get lost.

The things I’d most like to hear are:

* **What did you try, and how did it go?**
* **Where did you get confused or stuck?**
* **Did anything break or behave differently from what you expected?**
* **What felt good, and what felt annoying?**
* **Was there anything you’d come back to use?**
* **What feels missing?**

You don’t need to write a formal bug report. Something like “I tried Expert on my phone and the board was awkward to navigate” is useful. If something breaks, your device/browser and what you did just before it happened would help. Screenshots are welcome if they’re easy to grab.

Replies here are fine. There’s also a private support inbox through Account if you’d prefer to report a site problem there.

I’ve put a lot into this, but I need other people’s perspectives to understand what’s working and what needs attention. You don’t have to know anything about development to help.

**If you give it a try, thank you. And if you get stuck, please tell me. That’s exactly the kind of thing I’m asking for help finding.**

[**minesweeper.life**](https://minesweeper.life/)

\-Michael
